title: Barcoding Protocol for Microalgae
author: Elena L. Peredo
materials: https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/F160S Use the Dilution & Storage protocol as follows: Take a colony or an aliquot of culture (enough to see a small pellet in the tube) and place it in 20 μL of Dilution Buffer (use PCR tubes). You can crush the sample with a pipette tip by briefly pressing it against the tube wall. Heat the sample to 95°C for 2 minutes and then store it at 4°C overnight before proceeding with PCR. Before usage, you can crush the sample with a pipette tip again. This step aids in breaking the cells. If a larger amount of sample is used, increase the volume of Dilution Buffer to 50 μL. The solution should appear greenish. Spin down the plant material, and use 0.5-1 μL of the supernatant as a template in a 20 μL PCR reaction. The required volume of the supernatant may vary depending on the plant material used and the volume used for the dilution. Volumes Thermocycler program.

ExoSAP-IT: To use ExoSAP-IT, follow these steps: Dilute the ExoSAP-IT enzyme in molecular-grade H2O at a ratio of 1:4 (0.25 μl enzyme in 0.75 μl water). Add 1 μl of the diluted ExoSAP-IT mix to 1-2 μl of your PCR product. (For my application, I use 2 μl of the PCR product and 1 μl of the diluted enzyme mix, and it works well for me). Place 1 μl of the mixture at the side of each well on a sequencing plate, then add your PCR reaction and mix by pipetting. Briefly spin down the plate to ensure all wells are properly filled. Since the PCR product is green, visual inspection is quick. Seal the plate and run the enzyme protocol in the thermocycler. Due to the enzyme dilution, I use slightly longer times: 30 minutes at 37°C, followed by 15 minutes at 80°C, and then hold at 4°C.

steps.title: Set up 18S/ITS PCR
steps.instruction: Combine the following in a PCR tube to a final volume of 20 µl: 1 µl extracted DNA, 10 µl 1X GoTaq® Green Master Mix (catalog M712), 0.4 µl forward primer (10 µM), 0.4 µl reverse primer (10 µM), 1 µl DMSO, and 7.2 µl nuclease‑free water. Run a touchdown PCR: start annealing at 63 °C and decrease the annealing temperature by 0.5 °C each cycle for 12 cycles, then continue with 25 cycles at 55 °C.

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1.5 % agarose gel. Mix 7 µl of the PCR product with 2 µl of 1:1000 SYBR® Safe dye (loading dye is already present in GoTaq). Load the mixture into a well and run the gel to verify amplification and product size.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing PCR
steps.instruction: For each well add the BPC sequencing reaction mix using a 10 µM primer (instead of the usual 15 µM). After ExoSAP‑IT cleanup assume the template volume is 2 µl (not 3 µl). In each well combine: 0.5 µl X1BDT, 0.4 µl 5X buffer, 0.4 µl primer (10 µM), 0.1 µl DMSO, 2 µl H₂O, and the 2 µl template already present. Choose one of the primer pairs listed below for the sequencing reaction.

substeps.instruction: Primer pair options: SSU1/C18G or N18J/C18J.
